title: /api/trade/suggestions emits two different value concepts under one field name, showing Travis Hunter at 5,637 on /trade while /rankings shows 4,401
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'The whole trick is that every engine reads exactly one value - rankDerivedValue' (src/league_intel/overlay.py:17-21), and stage 11 two-way boost is 'A genuine post-blend OVERRIDE: rankDerivedValue becomes max(offense value, alt-position-family value)'.
observed: suggestions.py READS rankDerivedValue at intake (:561) but RE-SERIALIZES it from offense_only_value whenever _trade_is_idp_free(give, receive) is true (_serialize_suggestion :1762 -> _serialize_player :1737-1741). Both concepts ship under the same key 'displayValue'. On the live payload 19 of 51 asset legs across all 12 teams disagree with the board in DEFAULT market mode. Worst case Travis Hunter: the offense-only board never saw the two-way boost, so /trade shows 5,637 while /rankings shows 4,401. The same player can carry two different displayValues inside ONE response - Brian Thomas appears at 4,436 in one suggestion leg and 4,466 in rosterAnalysis.byPosition.

reproduction.expected: every displayValue equals the row's rankDerivedValue
reproduction.actual: market mode : 19/51 legs disagree with rankDerivedValue; worst: Travis Hunter shown=5637 board=4401 (+28.08%)

numericProof.formula: displayValue = offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue when _trade_is_idp_free else rankDerivedValue; pct = (5637-4401)/4401*100

userImpact: A user reading a sell-high suggestion on /trade sees Travis Hunter valued 28% above the board that /rankings, /rosters, the TradeMeter and every team total use. Accepting a package built on that number gives away ~1,236 board points of surplus. 19 of 51 legs are wrong by some amount with no indication which value concept is on screen.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A20-F06 identified the overlay/offense-only scale mix as a leagueAdjusted problem. This finding shows the SAME mechanism is already wrong in DEFAULT market mode, independent of any lens, and that the two-way boost (stage 11) is silently reverted on a user-facing surface - which PRIOR-A08-F01/A11-F07 examined only as a math/test-coverage question.

whatWorks: finder.py made this migration correctly: metadata.valueSource is stamped 'rankDerivedValue' on a live probe and unpriced assets are counted rather than dropped silently.
rootCause: The offense-only board is a legitimate second value concept (an IDP-disabled re-run of the pipeline) but it is serialized into the field name the board value owns, so the response has no way to say which concept a number belongs to.
requiredRepair: Either (a) drop the offense_only branch in _serialize_player and always emit rankDerivedValue, keeping offense-only for the internal _eff_val gap math only, or (b) emit it as a distinct key (offenseOnlyDisplayValue) plus a per-suggestion valueBasis stamp, and have trade-sections.jsx render the board value. Special-case the two-way players: max(offense, alt) must not be discardable by an offense-only re-read.
dependencies: Fixing this also removes most of W29-F002's surface.

title: valuationMode=leagueAdjusted is stamped on responses where 41% of asset legs are still priced on the unadjusted market board
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Mechanism, in one place: server.py::_valuation_scoped_contract fetches the league's factors and hands the engine a contract whose playersArray rows are already repriced. No engine knows the feature exists, because every engine reads exactly one value.' And: 'Every response stamps valuationMode - including "market". "This is the market board" and "this field is missing" must not read the same.'
observed: overlay.adjusted_rows multiplies exactly one field: copy['rankDerivedValue'] = round(base*factor) (overlay.py:90-93). offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue is copied through unchanged. Because suggestions.py serializes all-offense trades from that field (W29-F001), 21 of 51 legs (41.2%) across all 12 teams come back at the unadjusted market value while the response header says valuationMode: leagueAdjusted. For the 'Jason' roster it is 12 of 12 - the entire suggestion set. The same response's rosterAnalysis block IS adjusted, so one screen mixes both boards. The client-side applier is inconsistent with the server one: dynasty-data.js:1946-1948 additionally scales values.overall/finalAdjusted/displayValue and :1980 _finalAdjusted.

reproduction.expected: 0 legs at the unadjusted value when valuationMode=leagueAdjusted
reproduction.actual: adjusted : 21/51 legs still at the UNADJUSTED offense-only market value

userImpact: A user who switches to the league-adjusted board gets trade suggestions priced on the market board, labelled adjusted, sitting on the same screen as a roster analysis that IS adjusted. The stated purpose of the lens - 'adjusted rankings, market-priced trades, in the same session, with nothing on screen saying so' - is the exact condition still present, now with a label asserting otherwise.

priorFinding.note: Prior identified the mechanism by code reading. Reproduced here at runtime across all 12 rosters with per-leg arithmetic: 21/51 legs, and 12/12 for one roster. Prior did not measure blast radius or note that the response stamps the mode it is not honouring.

whatWorks: The lens itself is real and correct where it applies: 709/1092 rows carry a factor, monotonicityViolations is empty, and Jayden Daniels moves 8898 -> 9061 exactly as factor 1.018366 predicts. adjusted_rows correctly returns ALL rows rather than compact_ranks_and_tiers' ranked subset.
rootCause: The overlay was written against the invariant 'every engine reads exactly one value'. That invariant is false for suggestions.py, and nothing enforces it - tests/api/test_valuation_mode_threading.py checks that handlers STAMP the mode, not that the served numbers moved.
requiredRepair: Scale offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue by the same factor in overlay.adjusted_rows (and mirror _offenseOnlyFinalAdjusted), OR remove the offense-only serialization per W29-F001. Add an assertion to the threading test that at least one served value differs between modes for a roster with known non-unit factors.

title: exports/latest/dynasty_full.csv publishes the scraper composite under the column name 'Composite'; 804 of 805 rows disagree with the board the site shows
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'The live /api/data contract is the single source of truth'. exports/latest/ is the released artifact set (141 tracked files).
observed: dynasty_full.csv's Composite column is _finalAdjusted, which Dynasty Scraper.py:7128 sets directly from _composite - the raw pre-Hill scraper blend. It is not the board. Matching the 1,074 CSV rows against the live contract: 805 players match by name, exactly 1 has an identical value, median ratio composite/board = 1.0855 with p10 0.956 and p90 1.260. The disagreement is not a constant rescale, so it cannot be corrected by a factor: QBs and IDP read low (Lamar Jackson 7,631 vs 8,784; Carson Schwesinger 4,357 vs 5,908) while others read high.

reproduction.expected: CSV values equal the board values shown on /rankings

userImpact: Anyone who takes dynasty_full.csv as the site's values - the obvious reading of a file named dynasty_full with a column named Composite - trades against numbers up to 26% away from what the site shows. No HTTP route serves the file (openapi.json has only /api/public/league/{section}.csv and /api/trade/export-ktc), so reach is limited to whoever opens the repo or the release bundle.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A25-F15 mentions dynasty_full.csv only as a path that a different audit script fails to find. No prior compares its contents to the board.

whatWorks: Every in-app export agrees with the screen. /rankings' Export CSV and Copy values both go through buildExportLines using the identical expression as the render (rankings/page.jsx:764 vs :1050). dynasty_values.csv is per-source raw vendor values and is correctly labelled Player,KTC,IDPTradeCalc.
rootCause: The CSV writers live in Dynasty Scraper.py and predate the canonical pipeline. They emit what the scraper knows; nothing re-writes them from the contract after _compute_unified_rankings runs.
requiredRepair: Either rename the column to RawComposite and add a Board column populated from the contract, or regenerate the file from latest_contract_data after the contract build. Renaming alone is the smaller correct change.

title: Every visible trade-history grade is today's board applied retroactively to trades up to a year old; the as-of path exists but only drives a secondary badge and is dead without rank_history.jsonl
claimUnderTest: frontend/lib/trade-retro-value.js:1-8: 'The existing analyzeSleeperTradeHistory grades trades at *current* values. This helper layers in the at-trade snapshot so the UI can show a trade's age.' frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:392: 'Rank history lets each trade be valued at the date it happened.'
observed: resolveTradeItemValue reads row.values.full - today's board - for players (:146) and for picks (:132). Everything a user reads is built from it: pctGap, the letter grade, the 'won by X%' headline (trades/page.jsx:264) and the teamScores won/lost/totalGain leaderboard (:552-573). gradeRetro IS wired with asOfMs but produces only an aged_well/aged_poorly/stable badge, never the headline. Its own at-trade leg has two holes: picks always take the current value by design (trade-retro-value.js:76-83, source 'current'), and trades predating coverage fall back to the earliest sample (pointAt :52-56). Live contract carries 110 trades spanning 2025-08-05 to 2026-07-31; 24% of the 1,002 traded assets are picks and 60% of trades contain at least one. In this container the badge is inert: data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist and GET /api/data/rank-history?days=365 returns {"days":365,"history":{}}, so every asset takes current_fallback and verdictDelta is identically 0.

reproduction.expected: populated per-player history so gradeRetro can value assets at the trade date
reproduction.actual: {"days":365,"history":{}} and 'ls: cannot access data/rank_history.jsonl: No such file or directory'

userImpact: Every 'A+ / won by 38%' verdict and the whole manager win/loss leaderboard on /trades is hindsight. A manager who traded for a player who later broke out is scored as prescient; the counterparty is scored as fleeced, when at the time the deal may have been even. Nothing on the page discloses the as-of basis.

priorFinding.note: Prior identified the hindsight grade and the badge-not-grade structure by code reading. Added here: runtime proof the retro path is currently inert (rank_history.jsonl absent, endpoint returns an empty history object), and the pick share that the retro path can never fix even when populated - 24% of assets, 60% of trades.

whatWorks: The as-of machinery is genuinely built and correctly shaped: pointAt picks the closest-before sample, valueFromPoint prefers the server-stamped canonical val over a local Hill approximation, and data/source_value_history.jsonl exists with a documented 180-snapshot retention.
rootCause: gradeRetro was layered on as an enhancement rather than substituted into analyzeRawTrade, so the correct valuation never reaches the number the user reads.
requiredRepair: Make the at-trade valuation the primary grade when history covers the trade date, and label the current-value number explicitly as 'today'. Stamp per-item source (rankHistory | current_fallback) on the rendered grade so a partially-covered trade says so. Ensure rank_history.jsonl is produced in production. Pick history is the real gap - either persist pick values per snapshot or exclude pick-bearing trades from the graded leaderboard.
dependencies: Requires rank_history.jsonl to be written by the scrape/refresh path.

title: The 'Seller cash-out' tag compares a 0-9999 board value against a 0-100 ROS index and is unreachable for all 1,092 rows
claimUnderTest: src/api/gameplan.py:34-38: 'Two scales that must never be mixed - rosValue (0-100, rest-of-season STRENGTH INDEX) and canonicalSiteValues (0-9999, dynasty market) are different currencies with no validated conversion between them.'
observed: The predicate is `dynastyValue < rosValue * 0.7` with `isStrong` requiring rosValue >= 60, and dynastyValue supplied as `row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue` (PlayerPopup.jsx:142) - the 0-9999 board. Live /api/ros/player-values gives max rosValue 86.79, so the right-hand side maxes at 60.8. The live board's minimum rankDerivedValue is 757. The two ranges do not overlap: 0 of 1,092 rows can satisfy it. The tag has never rendered. The same predicate is duplicated in three places (two JS, one Python).

reproduction.expected: some players qualify for the 'Seller cash-out' tag
reproduction.actual: max(rosValue*0.7)=60.8  min(rankDerivedValue)=757  rows able to fire: 0

userImpact: A veteran with strong short-term value and a collapsed dynasty price - exactly the sell-now case the tag exists to surface - is never flagged, on the popup and on the /trade RosTradeFitPanel. Silent absence, not a wrong number.

priorFinding.note: Also PRIOR-A02-F06 (RosTradeFitPanel copy) and PRIOR-A19-F13 (src/ros/tags.py original). All three describe the same predicate in three locations. Reproduced here against the live /api/ros/player-values max (86.79) and the live board minimum (757) rather than against source constants, and counted the affected rows at exactly 0 of 1,092.

whatWorks: src/api/gameplan.py deliberately withholds site_values from the ROS target engines for precisely this reason and documents that feeding them 0-9999 numbers would return an edge of ~-0.99 for every player. The firewall is right; these three tag call sites are the leak.
rootCause: The predicate was written against a percentile-like dynasty value and the call sites now pass the raw board value. Duplicating it into three files made the mismatch survive review three times.
requiredRepair: Convert one side before comparing - e.g. compare dynasty percentile rank against ROS percentile rank - and collapse the three copies to one shared helper. Add a unit test asserting the tag fires on a constructed case, which would have caught this at zero cost.

title: REFUTED: the /rankings Value column does not fall back to the raw scraper composite - the values.* trio is null exactly when rankDerivedValue is null
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A01-F00 (severity critical): 'The Value column silently switches from the Hill-curve board to the raw scraper composite for 260 rows, and 158 of them display a LARGER number than the deepest genuinely-priced player', citing Devin Bush as values={overall:2549, finalAdjusted:2549, displayValue:null}.
observed: Does not reproduce on this build. data_contract.py:9229-9236 writes overall, finalAdjusted and displayValue together in one branch gated on `rdv is not None and rdv > 0`, and leaves all three null otherwise. Live payload: 0 rows have displayValue null while overall or finalAdjusted is non-null; 280 rows have the whole trio null. Devin Bush reads values={overall:null, finalAdjusted:null, displayValue:null, rawComposite:2544} and rankDerivedValue:null. Simulating _materializePlayerArrayRow exactly over all 1,092 rows: 0 rows would display a non-zero value while rankDerivedValue is null. The prior's evidence cites exports/latest/dynasty_data.js - the SCRAPER output, where _finalAdjusted is present on all 1,074 rows - not the contract, which nulls the values.* trio. The two were conflated. Related: PRIOR-A09-F07 ('values.displayValue is read by two modules and produced by none') is also refuted - it is produced at data_contract.py:9233 and is non-null on 812 rows. Only _canonicalDisplayValue is unproduced, and nothing reads it any more (dynasty-data.js:156 records this).

reproduction.actual: rows with values.displayValue null but overall/finalAdjusted set: 0 (prior claimed 260)

numericProof.formula: count(rows where values.displayValue is null AND (values.overall is not null OR values.finalAdjusted is not null))

userImpact: None. Unpriced rows display 0 and sort to the bottom, which is the intended behaviour.

priorFinding.note: Not reproducible on HEAD e96c06ef / contract 2026-03-10.v2. Either the guard at data_contract.py:9229 landed after the prior audit, or the prior read the scraper export rather than the contract. Reported so a P0-shaped claim is not carried forward unverified. PRIOR-A09-F07 refuted on the same evidence.

whatWorks: The scale-contract comment block at dynasty-data.js:140-157 is accurate: raw and full are held apart, an unpriced row reports 0 and drops out of sums rather than contributing a composite-scale number.
rootCause: n/a - prior finding does not reproduce.
requiredRepair: None. Keep the single-branch write at data_contract.py:9229-9236; splitting it is what would reintroduce the prior's scenario.

title: The league-adjusted board's scarcity is measured entirely in ROS log-rank units, so a 0-100 ordinal index sets the multiplier on every dynasty trade value under the adjusted lens
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the valuation overlay is driven by 'positional scarcity from this league's 12 rosters'. It does not say the scarcity is measured in ROS units.
observed: compute_scarcity reads value = float(p.get('rosValue')) for every rostered player (replacement.py:631) out of data/ros/team_strength/<league>.json, and measure_endogenous_starters solves the lineup over the same field. lineupScarcity is a RATIO of two rosValues, so it is dimensionless and no scale is mixed - but rosValue is 100*(ln(N+1)-ln(r))/ln(N+1), an ordinal log-rank index (ros/aggregate.py:171, gameplan.py:40-49). A ratio of two ordinal indices is not a cardinal 'drop from the top player to the last starter'. That ratio becomes factor = 1 + (lineupScarcity - 0.5)*0.20 (adjustment.py:247) and multiplies every dynasty value the engines serve. Live: WR lineupScarcity 0.634 -> factor 1.0268; DL 0.767 -> 1.0978; LB 0.598 -> 0.9797. replacement.py:20-52 documents the known bias honestly (projection path measures FLEX-TE share at 0.0% vs 10.4% on weekly actuals) but the docstring lives on the measurement function, not on the published board.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w29.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/valuation/league-adjusted | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print({k:round(v['lineupScarcity'],4) for k,v in d['scarcity'].items()}); print({k:d['factors'][k] for k in list(d['factors'])[:4]})"
reproduction.expected: scarcity documented as derived from a cardinal value scale
reproduction.actual: lineupScarcity values 0.436-0.767 are ratios of rosValue, a 0-100 ordinal log-rank index; factors 0.953-1.043 multiply the 0-9999 board

userImpact: A user selecting the adjusted board gets every trade value multiplied by a number derived from rest-of-season ordinal ranks. The direction is plausible and bounded (MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT 0.25, observed +-4.5%), but the quantity is not the cardinal scarcity the name implies, and the /rankings toggle says nothing about ROS being its input.

priorFinding.note: Priors reference rosValue scale mixing at the tag call sites (A01-F14 / A02-F06 / A19-F13) but none trace rosValue through compute_scarcity into the adjusted board that the engines serve.

whatWorks: The coupling is dimensionally SAFE - a ratio of rosValues cancels units, so this is not the 0-9999-vs-0-100 error of W29-F005. Guardrails are real: evidence tier is STRUCTURAL_ONLY, absent axes contribute exactly 0, MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT clamps to +-25%, monotonicityViolations is empty on the live board, and docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md records that the adjusted board is deliberately a toggle rather than the default because four backtest framings found no improvement.
rootCause: ROS is the only per-player quantity the platform has that is defined over a full roster including bench, so it is the only thing an endogenous lineup solve can run on. That is a real constraint, not an oversight.
requiredRepair: Two separable steps. (1) Cheap and correct now: state the input in the overlay payload (a scarcityBasis: 'rosValue-ordinal' stamp) and in the /rankings toggle copy, so the lens does not read as board-derived. (2) The real fix: measure lineup scarcity from realized weekly scoring under the league's rate card - the same source scripts/measure_te_demand_actuals.py already uses - rather than from projection point estimates, which replacement.py itself shows understate flex demand for high-variance positions.
dependencies: Step 2 depends on weekly actuals coverage; src/bdvm/actuals.py already scores nflverse weekly rows under exact league settings.

title: trade-logic.js::displayValue ignores the user's per-player value override and its docstring describes a pick-year discount effectiveValue does not apply
claimUnderTest: trade-logic.js:192-201: 'Use this anywhere a row's "Our Value" number is shown (picker cells, sort comparators, headers). Don't use effectiveValue directly for display - it also applies the pick-year discount which is trade-math-only, not display.'
observed: effectiveValue (:181-185) applies no pick-year discount at all - it returns row.customValue when set, else row.values[valueMode]. The stated reason for displayValue's existence is therefore stale; the pick-year discount is applied in the backend pipeline (stage 12, config/weights/pick_year_discount.json) and is already baked into the value both functions read. The two functions now differ in exactly one way the docstring does not mention: displayValue (:203-209) never consults customValue, so a user's typed override drives the trade math but not any surface that renders through displayValue. Today the only displayValue call site is the search-results dropdown (trade-sections.jsx:118), which shows candidates before they are added and therefore before an override can exist - so the divergence is latent, not live.

reproduction.expected: effectiveValue applies a pick-year discount, per its own docstring
reproduction.actual: effectiveValue body is `if (row.customValue != null && row.customValue > 0) return row.customValue; return Number(row.values?.[valueMode] || 0);` - no discount term

numericProof.formula: count of pick-year-discount operations in effectiveValue body

userImpact: None today. The risk is the next call site: the docstring instructs developers to use displayValue for 'picker cells, sort comparators, headers', and any such use inside a side would render the pre-override number beside a total computed from the override.

priorFinding.note: No prior covers the effectiveValue/displayValue divergence or the stale discount rationale.

whatWorks: The override plumbing itself is clean: sidesWithOverrides (trade/page.jsx:534-544) copies rows rather than mutating, and every total, flow and Monte Carlo payload routes through effectiveValue so the override is applied consistently in the math.
rootCause: The pick-year discount moved into the backend pipeline and the client-side implementation was removed, but the docstring that justified the two-function split was not updated.
requiredRepair: Correct the docstring to state the real difference (customValue awareness), and make displayValue honour customValue so the two cannot diverge on a row inside a side. If a genuine 'show the board number, not the override' surface is wanted, name it that.
